output.summary: Yield loss is real (stable gauge R&R, customer PPM rising) and not explained by new operators (similar reject rates, decline began before they ran alone). Shift length, Corvane hardness scatter and deferred spindle service all changed within weeks of each other, and lots ran in sequence, so they are confounded. Scrap-tag timing is a batch-writing artifact, so it gives no fatigue evidence. Spindle runout rose on L3-02 and L3-05, but their tighter tolerance confounds that. The Plant Manager's 8-hour revert and the 1-in-10 sampling would act on an unconfirmed cause or remove a protective control. A staggered spindle service with Tamsworth trial lots, plus the Line 6 CMM data and cycle-counter matching, would separate the factors cheaply and reversibly.
